result.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in EventManager.ts: the DB fallback assigns `credential` only `if (credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug)`, and the subsequent `if (credential)` guard then silently skips `createEvent` with no log or calWarning. So a credential row lacking an app relation results in a booking with no calendar event and zero signal — a real silent-failure path introduced by this diff, though the prevalence of app-less credentials can't be confirmed from the diff alone.

judged_text: The DB credential fallback is gated on `credentialFromDB.app?.slug`, so any credential row whose app relation is absent (legacy/seeded credentials or credentials created before the app-store migration) is skipped and the destination is silently not created against. Bookings for such credentials complete without a calendar event and without any logged error or user-facing warning, because the `if (credential)` guard simply skips the createEvent call; operators debugging missing calendar events get no signal that the credential was dropped here.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination has `credentialId` but it isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, the new DB fallback only constructs a usable `credential` if `credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug` (see `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}})` and the subsequent `if (credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug) { credential = { appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug, ... } }`). If `app` is null/undefined (or `slug` missing), `credential` remains undefined and the code silently skips `createEvent` because it is guarded by `if (credential) { ... }` with no logging/alerting in that branch. The diff doesn’t prove such legacy credentials exist, but the skip-without-signal behavior is directly verifiable from the added logic and is an important edge case/regression risk.
